text.p: - The last round of talks between Slovenia and NATO ended in Brussels on Monday. NATO is next year expected to decide whether Slovenia will be in the first group of countries that will be accepted in the 16-member military pact.
- In the latest Euromoney country risk rating Slovenia rose 12 places to rank 34th, after Kuwait and in front of the Czech Republic.
- Slovenian employers pushed for cuts in work benefits, claiming the cost of the workforce is hampering competitiveness of Slovenian companies.
- The annual inflation rate fell to 9.4 percent in September from 10.3 percent in August.
- Slovenian Payment Agency said it would reduce its prices by an average of 32 percent. The reduction has to be approved by the government.

- The current finance minister and two former finance ministers filed complaints to the Constitutional Court over the report of a parliamentary investigating committee that said the ministers may have abused their authority when dealing with casino firm Hit.
- The law on the use of agricultural land expires on October 13, although the parliament may not have enough time to pass the newly prepared substitute law by then.

- Central bank governors from Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Macedonia met in Washington on Monday and said they all support the Bank for International Settlement proposal over the division of assets of former Yugoslavia.
